subject: Information Theory
title: Fact-Checking at Scale
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Fact-Checking at Scale.

hook.text: Facebook employs thousands of fact-checkers covering 60 languages. They can't keep up. Generation outpaces verification.

buildup.text: Automated fact-checking uses NLP to compare claims against trusted databases. Speed helps, but accuracy is imperfect.

discovery.text: The fundamental asymmetry: creating a false claim takes seconds. Verifying it can take hours of research.

twist.text: Adding a fact-check label can backfire: it implies unchecked content is true. Absence of a label becomes endorsement.

climax.text: The information-theoretic challenge: verification capacity is far below generation capacity. The channel is overwhelmed.

punchline.text: Anyone can claim. Few can verify. The asymmetry is structural.

quiz.question: Why can't fact-checking fully solve misinformation?
options: False claims are generated far faster than they can be verified
